scope: Rename the shared execution engine to SchedulerRuntime, move its module/implementation into runtime, expose three concrete policy module entries, and document actual SMP behavior

smp.runtime_service: One shared statically constructed runtime; each hart owns its run-loop context, CpuState and scheduler stack
smp.ready_structure: Shared selected-policy tree/FIFO levels serialized by its queue lock
smp.handoff: Remove one queue item while locked, release queue lock, then acquire process lock before Running/current and swtch; outgoing owner releases the process lock after switching back
smp.fair_accounting: Monotonic floor includes all running entities with elapsed-time projection and pending yield entitlement
smp.affinity: Unbound work may migrate between harts; bound work is skipped by ineligible harts
smp.feedback: One global MLFQ boost epoch and shared FIFO levels; running entities are refreshed under the queue lock
smp.preemption: Each hart makes local timer preemption decisions; hart 0 also maintains global uptime/device service
smp.idle: Periodic local timer rechecks work; no cross-hart wake IPI, per-hart ready queues or work stealing
smp.scalability: Queue-lock contention and affinity scans remain; 1/5-hart checks are functional evidence, not a high-core scalability claim

dev_targeted.scope: Fair single/five-hart workloads plus process storage/groups/signals, trap and scheduling-model contracts

public_api_consumer.scope: Independent RISC-V module consumer compiles initialize(SchedulerKind::Fair)

renamed_symbols.scope: Final ELF contains SchedulerRuntime and all three policy types; old engine symbols absent

flow_source_bindings.caveat: Source/binding integrity is evidence of reviewed coverage, not proof of runtime semantics or every build profile.

validation.full_96_test_regression: Historical pre-rename result retained in previous checkpoint; this organization-only change used the targeted checks listed above
